McLaren.summary: McLaren has reshaped the front and rear “furniture” – the small aerodynamic pieces on the front‑corner, rear‑corner and engine‑cover – to smooth airflow and boost downforce, while a freshly‑cut side‑pod inlet and circuit‑specific cooling louvers keep the power unit running at optimal temperatures. A new floor layout and updated rear wing give extra grip at the rear, helping the car stick to the tarmac through high‑speed corners. Together, these tweaks should translate into quicker lap times and more consistent handling over the weekend’s demanding layout.

Mercedes F1 Team.summary: Mercedes have moved the rear‑pipe and fitted it with a new slotted bracket, a change that smooths the airflow and trims drag, giving the car a little extra bite on the straights. At the front, they’ve widened the lip on the front‑corner wing to better channel air, which should improve front‑end stability and grip through the corners. In short, the updates are designed to make the car faster on the straights while also giving it more confidence in the bends for this weekend’s race.

Red Bull Racing.summary: Red Bull have tweaked almost every aerodynamic hotspot on the RB 19 – a reshaped front wing, new front‑wheel bodywork, a re‑carved side‑pod inlet (with matching mirror brackets and engine‑cover tweaks), a cleaned‑up floor section and a revised rear‑corner layout – plus a fresh rear‑wing mounting that lets the straight‑line “DRS‑mode” deploy more reliably. All of these changes tighten the car’s airflow and boost downforce while shaving drag, meaning the car should be steadier through the corners and quicker on the straights this weekend. In short, it’s a full‑scale aero‑refresh aimed at squeezing out every extra tenth of a second on the track.

Scuderia Ferrari.summary: Ferrari’s new front wing end‑plate and front‑corner tweaks tighten up the airflow over the nose, giving the car a bit more front‑end grip right out of the box.  Revised floor panels, rear‑wing elements and cleaner‑shaped suspension fairings smooth the air under the car and cut drag, so the car can stay glued to the tarmac while still being quicker on the straights.  In short, the updates should boost corner speed and improve overall balance for the weekend’s tracks.

Williams Racing.summary: Williams has reshaped almost every rear‑end surface – the floor, side‑pods, engine cover, cooling exits, mirrors, tail‑pipe bracket, impact‑structure fairings and the rear‑brace wing – to match a new packaging layout. The tweaks clean up the airflow and improve cooling, giving the car a tighter rear aerodynamic platform and more stable handling on this weekend’s circuit. In short, the car should feel more planted and predictable through the fast corners, which could translate into better lap times and tyre life.

Racing Bulls / RB.summary: Racing Bulls have given the rear of the car a full‑on‑flow makeover – new brake‑duct shaping, re‑profiled rear‑wing and end‑plate sections, plus revised rear‑corner and suspension fairings – to smooth the air and add extra rear down‑force, helping the car stay glued through the fast, sweeping corners. At the front, a circuit‑specific flap option and reshaped wing‑end plates and flaps clean up the front‑end airflow, while subtle tweaks to the floor, diffuser and rear‑suspension improve under‑car flow and overall balance. Together these updates should tighten the car’s aerodynamic lock‑on, give more predictable grip and help the tyres last longer on this weekend’s high‑speed layout.

Haas F1 Team.summary: Haas has re‑tuned the rear diffuser to generate a bit more down‑force where the car is most sensitive, giving the rear a steadier grip through fast corners. The change should help the drivers keep the car planted on the current circuit’s high‑speed sections, translating into more confidence and potentially quicker lap times this weekend.

Audi F1 Team.summary: Audi’s new front brake duct and updated suspension covers tidy up airflow around the front wheels, giving the car a cleaner‑air package that improves grip off the line and through the corners. At the rear, a reshaped floor edge and a fresh diffuser winglet boost the car’s down‑force, helping it stick to the track and corner faster. Together, the changes should translate into better traction out of slow turns and higher cornering speeds for the upcoming race weekend.

Alpine F1 Team.summary: Alpine has refined the front of the car and the nose‑camera mounts to smooth the airflow off the front wheels, helping the car stay glued to the track. At the rear they’ve reshaped the suspension links, added a small reinforcement to the impact structure and fitted a brand‑new rear wing with a freshly shaped end‑plate, all to give extra grip and stability. Together, these tweaks should improve cornering confidence, tyre wear and overall pace, giving Alpine a stronger shot at points this weekend.
